title: PromQL AST String()/Pretty() rendering is slow due to fmt.Sprintf and per-call buffer churn on the hot path

source.license_note: Real upstream prometheus optimization PR #17067; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up the PromQL parser's expression-to-string rendering (Expr.String()/ShortString()/Pretty()) without changing the produced output.
task.instructions: Optimize the promql/parser package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkExprString measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: Expr.String()/ShortString() build output via fmt.Sprintf and allocate a fresh bytes.Buffer / intermediate strings per node, dominating CPU when rendering large PromQL expressions.

ops_fault.description: CPU profile of expression rendering shows fmt.Sprintf reflection and repeated buffer/string allocations dominating Expr.String() in promql/parser/printer.go.
detection_keywords: high CPU in String() hot path
repair_keywords: writeAggOpStr / writeLabels append to shared buffer

visible_context.issue_text: Rendering large PromQL expressions back to text via Expr.String() is unexpectedly slow and allocation-heavy, showing up in CPU profiles of rule/alert evaluation and API formatting.
error_logs: pprof: 41.2% cpu fmt.Sprintf -> reflect in promql/parser.(*AggregateExpr).String; BenchmarkExprString ~3200 ns/op, 18 allocs/op
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
